notes.note: Reviewed the kernel-required-test producer/consumer route. Main gained three Seatbelt tests without profile entries, so live classification failed in qualification 44236221383. All three are now mustPass, preserving every captured mandatory leg and both skip/not-required lists. The live profile covers 66 registrations (59 must-pass, five may-runtime-skip, two not-required); the pre-landing selector now runs the registration audit when either kernel producer changes. This audit filters out test bodies and checks identities only, not kernel behavior. The old 63-test macOS report is unchanged and paired with its historical profile for parser controls; the actual workflow still defaults to the live profile and correctly rejects that old report as missing three legs. No new kernel pass was fabricated. Local 89-test pass, downgrade fault failure, byte restoration and scripts typecheck are focused evidence; current 66-leg kernel execution and hosted qualification remain unverified.

Reviewed the two new supplemental selection edges from Seatbelt/bubblewrap process test files to check-required-tests-ran.test.ts. That suite collects registrations through a child process outside the import graph. Both real execution-selection cases failed on baseline and pass after the edges; related selection and broader lanes are retained. Existing context, verification, frontend/theming and scoped-instruction guidance still describes those unchanged rules. This adds an audit before landing without claiming Linux collection executes macOS kernel bodies.

Reviewed the added kernel-registration-audit explanation against the changed selector and collector. Existing development, code-quality, profile/fixture and scope instructions remain accurate: pre-landing identity checks are distinct from the actual main-only macOS kernel run and from hosted full qualification. The captured report/profile fixture documentation explicitly preserves historical scope rather than inventing new passing receipts.
